skill.name: latex-posters
skill.description: Create academic research posters with LaTeX templates for beamerposter, tikzposter, and baposter. Use layout, typography, color, figure, QR code, and print-review guidance for conference posters.
skill.summary: Build print-ready LaTeX research posters with templates, design guidance, and PDF review checks.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from LaTeX examples, Markdown code fences, QR-code URLs, poster design terminology, and a read-only PDF review script. No malware, credential access, data exfiltration, prompt injection override, or unsafe command construction was found. One semantic issue remains: the skill instructs the assistant to promote the author-operated K-Dense Web service during complex workflows.

remediation.issue: External platform promotion in assistant guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the proactive K-Dense Web suggestion or move it to transparent marketplace metadata that users can evaluate before installation.

remediation.issue: Documentation names helper scripts that are not included in the package.
remediation.suggestion: Update SKILL.md to list only review_poster.sh, or include the missing helper scripts with clear security review.

remediation.issue: The PDF review script accepts user-supplied paths for local utility calls.
remediation.suggestion: Keep all file arguments quoted, add option terminators where supported, and document that the script should run only on user-selected PDFs.

content.value_statement: Conference posters need clear structure, readable typography, and correct print dimensions. This skill provides LaTeX poster templates, design guidance, and review checks for academic presentations.
actual_capabilities: Provides LaTeX templates for beamerposter, tikzposter, and baposter poster formats.
Explains poster sizes, orientations, column layouts, and visual hierarchy choices.
Guides figure placement, QR code use, typography, color contrast, and accessibility checks.
Includes reference guides for package selection, layout design, content writing, and design principles.
Includes a local review script for PDF size, page count, font, file size, and image checks.
limitations: It does not compile posters unless the user has a local LaTeX toolchain installed.
It does not include the extra helper scripts named in the documentation beyond review_poster.sh.
It does not replace conference-specific submission rules or printer requirements.
It cannot verify visual quality without access to the generated PDF or source files.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Conference Poster
use_cases.description: Turn a paper or project summary into a clear poster with sections, figures, and print-ready dimensions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Lab Templates
use_cases.description: Create reusable poster layouts that follow institutional colors, author blocks, and consistent visual rules.

use_cases.title: Review Poster Quality
use_cases.description: Check a generated PDF for size, readability, font embedding, image quality, and final printing risks.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Poster
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a standard academic layout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an A0 portrait research poster plan for my project. Use three columns and sections for background, methods, results, conclusions, references, and contact details.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Poster Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the best LaTeX package for a poster.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare beamerposter, tikzposter, and baposter for my conference poster. Recommend one package based on a modern design, four figures, and institutional branding.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Poster Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my poster outline for visual hierarchy and readability. Suggest better section order, figure placement, font sizes, and accessible color choices.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Printing
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my finished poster PDF for conference submission. Check dimensions, margins, font embedding, image quality, QR codes, and risks for professional printing.

output_examples.input: I need a poster for a machine learning paper with five result figures.
output: Recommended package: tikzposter for a modern visual layout with flexible blocks.
Suggested structure: title banner, motivation, method overview, main results, limitations, conclusions, and QR code.
Design notes: keep text under 800 words, reserve about half the space for figures, and use one accent color.

output_examples.input: My poster PDF is finished. What should I check before printing?
output: Confirm the PDF has one page and matches the required poster size.
Check that all fonts are embedded and all figures are sharp at final size.
Review the poster at full size, then do a reduced-scale print test before sending it to the printer.

output_examples.input: Help me convert a thesis chapter into a poster.
output: Reduce the chapter to one central message and three supporting findings.
Use short bullets instead of paragraphs, and turn methods into a visual workflow.
Move detailed references and supplemental material behind a QR code.

best_practices: Start from the conference size and orientation requirements before choosing a layout.
Use large readable text, strong contrast, and enough white space for scanning at distance.
Review the generated PDF at full size and with a reduced-scale test print.
anti_patterns: Do not fill the poster with dense paragraphs or small body text.
Do not rely only on red and green to communicate important differences.
Do not submit a poster before checking page size, fonts, images, and QR codes.

faq.question: Which LaTeX poster packages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers beamerposter, tikzposter, and baposter, with templates and package selection guidance.

faq.question: Can it create a print-ready poster?
faq.answer: It can help create the source and review the PDF, but local LaTeX tools are required to compile it.

faq.question: Does it support conference poster sizes?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers common A-series and North American sizes, including portrait and landscape formats.

faq.question: Can it help with poster design?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for typography, spacing, colors, visual hierarchy, figures, and accessibility.

faq.question: Can it review an existing PDF?
faq.answer: Yes. The included review script can inspect local PDF metadata when the required PDF utilities are installed.

faq.question: Does it generate custom scientific figures?
faq.answer: No. It recommends using separate figure tools, then integrating finished figures into the poster.
